definition: Atrophy means to waste away or weaken from lack of use.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word atrophy. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know atrophy should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Critics wrote that the director's imagination had atrophied across a decade of sequels, each film a fainter tracing of the first.
Anything can weaken a little and recover by Friday; atrophy is heavier — a steady wasting that sets in when something goes unused.
Shrivel goes further than atrophy: an atrophied skill has thinned and faded, but a shriveled one has dried to a husk with almost nothing left to revive.

To wither is to dry up and shrivel under outside punishment — drought, frost, scorching heat — and, figuratively, to shrink under hostile pressure. Atrophy needs no attacker at all: the wasting comes from disuse alone — nothing attacks the thing; it simply goes unexercised.

To flag is to droop or lose vigor for a stretch — a runner's pace flags in the last mile, attention flags after lunch — a dip that passes when rest comes. Atrophy is slower and deeper: capacity wasting away over months of disuse, not sagging for an afternoon.

The airline's own data started the debate: captains with twenty years' experience were flying less accurately by hand than new hires.
Nobody's ability had been damaged, and no rule had changed; modern cockpits simply hand the routine flying to the autopilot.
